title: Terraform module: audit-log shipper (CloudTrail -> S3(KMS) -> OpenSearch ingest) with lifecycle and health checks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that configures end-to-end audit log shipping for Private/VPC deployments: enable CloudTrail, deliver events to a customer-configurable S3 bucket encrypted with KMS, lifecycle rules to tier to infrequent access and Glacier/Archive, and an optional OpenSearch ingest pipeline (Logstash/ingest nodes) with index lifecycle management. The module must support parameterized retention windows, cross-account delivery roles, and explicit upgrade/rollout semantics for on-prem and VPC installers. Provide automated health checks, TF state migration guidance, and patterns for safe encryption key rotation.
updates: 2026-02-18: Ticket created with initial RFC outline and architecture diagram attached to Confluence.

acceptance_criteria: Terraform module publishes to registry or internal module catalog with clear inputs/outputs and examples.
CloudTrail enabled and delivering events to the configured S3 bucket in test account using example variables.
S3 bucket has KMS encryption enabled, and key policy supports rotation without data loss.
Lifecycle rules enforce configurable retention windows and transition to Glacier/Archive for >90 days.
Optional OpenSearch ingest pipeline can be toggled; when enabled, events are indexed and ILM policies applied.
Automated health checks emit metrics to Prometheus/CloudWatch for: latest object age, delivery failures, OpenSearch ingest lag, and failed KMS decrypts.
Upgrade path documented: how to add module to existing stacks, handling of existing CloudTrail + S3 resources, and TF state import commands.
implementation_notes: Module inputs: cloudtrail_enabled (bool), s3_bucket_name (string OR generate), kms_key_id (optional), retention_days (int), enable_opensearch_ingest (bool), opensearch_endpoint (optional), cross_account_delivery_role_arn (optional).
Use aws_cloudtrail with event_selector that is configurable per-tenant; default to management events and write-only data events for S3 if enabled.
S3 lifecycle rules must use separate rules for transition vs expiration to satisfy AWS console and TF plan diffs.
KMS key: create symmetric CMK by default, but allow customers to pass an existing key ARN; rotate using separate rotation schedule resource and document key rotation steps.
OpenSearch: provide two integration options—direct index API (for private deployments with network access) or an S3 -> Logstash pipeline for air-gapped clusters.
Ensure IAM roles/policies are minimal-privilege; include example principal ARNs for cross-account delivery and instructions for Organizations delegation.
Document known limitations: S3 object-level logs vs CloudTrail data events, eventual consistency leading to small delivery lag, and region-bound OpenSearch clusters.
test_plan: Unit tests: TF validate and tfsec static checks in CI for every PR.
Integration: provision module into ephemeral dev account, run CloudTrail events (console login, S3 PUT) and assert objects arrive and OpenSearch indices are created.
Chaos test: simulate permission denial on delivery role to ensure alerting and graceful retry behavior are surfaced by health checks.
Upgrade test: import existing S3 and CloudTrail resources into TF state and run module apply to validate idempotent changes.
Performance: generate 10k small events and measure OpenSearch ingest lag and S3 put throughput; tune batching settings in the ingest pipeline.
